papers.title: The effect of health insurance expansion on price and demand for medications among the uninsured.
papers.abstract: Social health insurance expansions can affect not only new beneficiaries but also those who remain outside the program. This paper studies these spillovers in the context of Medicare Part D. Increases in insured demand can raise or lower price depending on market conditions: they may increase price when pharmaceutical firms face less elastic demand, but reduce price when demand concentration strengthens bargaining and pass-through in competitive markets. I find that Part D lowered the out-of-pocket unit price paid by Americans under age 65 without prescription drug insurance. Price declines are larger in therapeutic classes more exposed to Part D and in classes with stronger within-class competition, consistent with a demand-concentration channel. Demand increases mainly for generic drugs and among existing users. The implied consumer-surplus gain is roughly $76 per person per year, comprising about $65 from lower price on inframarginal consumption and $11 from additional consumption. Demand responses appear strongest among lower-income, younger, and healthier uninsured individuals, consistent with greater pre-existing non-adherence. Although price fall across several drug classes, demand does not increase significantly for medications associated with greater overuse in the United States, suggesting potentially positive net health spillovers.
papers.summary: 本文探討聯邦醫療保險D部分（Medicare Part D）的擴張對無處方藥保險者的溢出效應。研究發現，保險需求增加帶來的需求集中效應增強了議價能力，從而降低了65歲以下無保險者的藥品自付單價，此現象在競爭較強的治療類別中尤為顯著。此外，藥品需求增加主要集中在學名藥與既有使用者，且以較低收入、較年輕及較健康的無保險者反應最為強烈；而容易過度使用的藥物需求並未顯著增加。
papers.significance: 此研究揭示了健康保險政策不僅影響直接受保人，還會透過改變市場需求結構對未參保者產生正向的價格溢出效應。其證明在競爭市場中，需求集中能有效促進價格下降並帶來實質的消費者剩餘（每人每年約76美元）。更重要的是，需求增加未發生在易被濫用的藥物上，暗示該政策不僅具有經濟效益，還可能產生改善用藥依從性的正向淨健康外部性，對後續醫保政策的全面評估具有重要參考價值。
